c.tagline: Nepal's Terai gateway to Lumbini, birthplace of the Buddha.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis and auto-rickshaws are unmetered, so agree the fare before setting off; the Pathao and InDrive apps work in the Bhairahawa area and help fix a fair price.

emergency.note: 100 reaches the Nepal Police, 102 is the ambulance service, and 101 is the fire brigade; 1144 is a national tourist/traffic hotline.

avoid.reason: Watch for touts, rigged money-changers and overcharging rickshaws around the Sunauli/Belahiya India border crossing.

hood_desc: The busy commercial heart of Bhairahawa, packed with shops, hotels, money changers, and eateries; the practical base for travelers using the city as a launchpad to Lumbini and the Indian border.
A major crossroads and dining-and-shopping hub of the city, lively in the evenings with restaurants, sweet shops, and street food; good for travelers who want food and buzz near their hotel.
A central commercial junction lined with markets, textile and electronics shops, and local bazaars; suits shoppers and those wanting an everyday-Nepal Terai street scene.

The UNESCO-listed Sacred Garden 25 km west, where the Maya Devi Temple marks the Buddha's birthplace beside the Ashoka Pillar, sacred pond, and the international Monastic Zone of temples; the reason most visitors come, best for pilgrims and a peaceful overnight.
The border settlement 4 km south where Nepal meets Sunauli in India, a transit point of guesthouses, exchange counters, and bus stands; a functional, quieter base mainly for overland crossers.

water.note: Drink only bottled, boiled, or purified water throughout Nepal's Terai.

transit.hours: Auto-rickshaws, shared tempos, and buses run from early morning to mid-evening; after dark, private taxis and app rides are the main option.
transit.note: There is no metro or rail. Getting around is by auto-rickshaw, shared electric/diesel tempos, cycle-rickshaws, local buses, and taxis; Lumbini is reached by taxi, bus, or hired auto from the city.
transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash (Nepalese rupees) directly to the driver; shared tempos have fixed low fares while taxis and autos are negotiated. No transit card exists.

bus: Intercity buses to Kathmandu, Pokhara and Butwal
Local buses, shared tempos and auto-rickshaws to Lumbini and the border
train: No passenger rail in the city; the nearest Indian railhead is Nautanwa, across the border

airport.name: Gautam Buddha International Airport (BWA)
rentals: Local car and taxi hire operators

transit.m: Auto-rickshaw / shared tempo to the bazaar (10-15 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving about 10% at tourist restaurants and tipping guides and drivers is appreciated.
